extraction_notes: Cl2 — halogen element. Ch.28 Note 1 covers separate chemical elements.
I2 — purple-black crystalline halogen, sublimes.
F2 — most electronegative element, pale-yellow gas.
Br2 — dark-red liquid halogen at room temperature.
Flowers of sulphur — distilled fine yellow powder (S8). Heading 2802 covers sublimed/precipitated/colloidal sulphur; crude sulphur is in Ch.25.
Milk of sulphur — precipitated from polysulphide solution; very fine amorphous S.
Colloidal S — ultra-fine particles in aqueous suspension, pharmaceutical/dermatological use.
Furnace/channel black — amorphous carbon. Ch.28 covers carbon blacks; carbon other than diamond/graphite.
Acetylene black — high-purity carbon black from C2H2 decomposition; high electrical conductivity.
Other carbon black variants in heading 2803.
H2 — lightest gas; key feedstock for NH3 (Haber) and petroleum refining.
Ar — chemically inert noble gas, most-used shielding gas in TIG/MIG welding.
He — second-lightest element; sole cryogen below 4.2 K for superconducting magnets.
Other rare gases — neon, krypton, xenon, radon.
N2 — 78% of air; liquid N at 77 K used as cryogen.
Medical O2 — pharmacopoeia-grade for inhalation/anaesthesia.
O2 — industrial/welding grade.
B — metalloid; p-type semiconductor dopant; high neutron-capture cross-section.
Te — silvery-white metalloid used in CdTe solar cells.
Electronic-grade Si — >=99.99% purity; subheading note specifies threshold.
Metallurgical-grade Si — below electronic-grade purity threshold.
Black phosphorus — most stable allotrope; 2D semiconductor material.
Red P — amorphous, less reactive than white; used on matchbox strikers.
White/yellow P (P4) — highly toxic and pyrophoric; stored under water.
As — toxic metalloid; key dopant for n-type GaAs.
Se — photoconductive non-metal; used in photocopier drums and CIGS solar.
Na metal — soft silvery alkali metal; stored under kerosene to prevent reaction with moisture/air.
Ca metal — alkaline-earth metal; key reductant for production of uranium/thorium.
Other Group-1/Group-2 metals — lithium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, strontium, barium, etc.
Lanthanides plus Sc and Y — 'whether or not intermixed or interalloyed' wording covers mischmetal too.
Hg — only metal liquid at room temperature. Subject to Minamata Convention restrictions.
HCl — strong mineral acid; commercial 'muriatic acid' is ~37% aqueous solution.
ClSO3H — primary sulphonating agent for alkylbenzene sulphonates (detergents).
Oleum — H2SO4 with free SO3 dissolved; far more aggressive sulphonating agent than plain sulphuric acid.
HNO3 — strong oxidising acid; key precursor to ammonium nitrate and TNT.
Nitrating acid — H2SO4+HNO3 mixture used in aromatic nitration (TNT, nitroglycerine).
P2O5 — most powerful desiccant; hygroscopic white solid that violently absorbs water.
H3PO4 — also spelled 'phosporic' in the tariff line (sic).
PPA — pyro-/meta-/poly- condensed phosphoric acids; viscous syrups used in organic cyclisations.
B2O3 — boric anhydride; principal glass flux ingredient.
H3BO3 — weak acid; mild antiseptic and roach killer.
HF — extremely hazardous; only acid that etches glass; key precursor to fluorocarbons.
HCN — extremely toxic; covered as inorganic acid in Ch.28 per Note 1(a). Synthesised industrially via Andrussow process.
H3PO2 — strong reducing agent; only one P-H bond ionisable.
H3AsO4 / H3AsO3 — toxic; used in wood preservation (CCA-treated lumber).
Tariff-line 'sulphonic acid' in heading 2811 refers to sulphamic acid (H3NSO3) — inorganic. Organic sulphonic acids belong to Ch.29.
Other inorganic acids of non-metals not separately specified.
Dry ice — solid CO2 at -78.5 deg C; sublimes directly to gas.
CO2 gas or liquid — non-dry-ice forms.
SiO2 — synthetic silica (silica gel, fumed silica, precipitated silica). Natural quartz is Ch.25.
As2O5 — anhydride of arsenic acid; highly toxic.
As2O3 — 'white arsenic'; classic poison; used in leukemia chemotherapy (Trisenox).
N2O — 'laughing gas'; dental anaesthetic and aerosol propellant.
CO — odourless toxic gas; component of syngas (Fischer-Tropsch feed).
SO3 — anhydride of H2SO4; reacts violently with water.
Other inorganic oxygen compounds of non-metals (selenium dioxide, antimony oxides not in 2825, etc.).
COCl2 — phosgene; CWA Schedule 3 chemical; key feedstock for TDI/MDI and polycarbonate via interfacial polymerisation.
POCl3 — converts -OH to -Cl in organic synthesis; used to make tricresyl phosphate.
PCl3 — primary precursor to glyphosate and many phosphites/phosphonates.
PCl5 — converts carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides.
S2Cl2 — golden-yellow oily liquid; cold-vulcanisation of rubber.
SCl2 — CWA Schedule 3 (Levinstein-process precursor to mustard agent).
SOCl2 — converts -OH or -COOH to chloride with gaseous SO2+HCl byproducts (clean).
SO2Cl2 — radical chlorinating agent in benzylic/allylic positions.
SiCl4 — fuming colourless liquid; key precursor for fumed silica (Cabot's process) and optical fibre preforms (MCVD/OVD).
AsCl3 — toxic liquid; CWA Schedule 2 (precursor to Lewisite).
Other halides/oxychlorides of non-metals.
Bromides/iodides/fluorides of non-metals (PBr3, PI3, BF3, SF6, etc.).
CS2 — volatile, highly flammable liquid; key cellulose-xanthation reagent for viscose.
As2S2 — synthetic realgar; orange-red pigment. Natural realgar is Ch.25.
P4S3 — sesquisulphide used on strike-anywhere match heads.
Calcium polysulphide solution — classic orchard fungicide/miticide; deep amber liquid.
Other sulphides of non-metals — P2S5, etc.
Anhydrous NH3 — Haber-Bosch product; backbone of fertiliser industry and most N chemistry.
Aqueous NH3 (ammonium hydroxide) — typically 25-30% w/w; safer to handle than anhydrous.
NaOH flakes — solid-form caustic soda from chlor-alkali; convenient solid handling.
Other solid NaOH forms (pellets, prills, lumps).
Soda lye / liquid caustic — 50% aqueous solution is industry-standard shipping form.
KOH — produces soft potassium soaps (vs hard sodium soaps); electrolyte in Ni-Cd and alkaline batteries.
Na2O2 / KO2 (superoxide) — generate O2 on contact with CO2; used in closed-circuit breathing apparatus.
Mg(OH)2 — 'milk of magnesia'; non-halogenated flame retardant in polymers.
MgO2 — slow-release O2 source; bioremediation of petroleum-contaminated soil.
SrO/BaO/Sr(OH)2/Ba(OH)2/SrO2/BaO2 — heavy alkaline-earth oxides/hydroxides/peroxides; BaO2 used in red pyrotechnics.
ZnO — white powder; major rubber-cure activator and physical UV sunscreen.
ZnO2 — yellowish powder; gentle antiseptic in skin preparations.
Synthetic Al2O3 corundum — electrofused from bauxite; Mohs 9 abrasive.
Smelter-grade calcined alumina meeting IS 17441 spec — feedstock for Hall-Heroult cells.
Non-metallurgical calcined alumina — high-purity ceramic/refractory grade.
Other aluminium oxide forms (activated alumina, alumina trihydrate, etc.).
Al(OH)3 / ATH — Bayer-process intermediate; halogen-free flame retardant in plastics.
CrO3 — dark-red crystals; Cr(VI) — REACH-restricted carcinogen; electroplating workhorse.
Cr2O3 / Cr(OH)3 — green pigment 'chrome green'; Cr(III) form, much less toxic than Cr(VI).
MnO2 — black solid; cathode in Leclanche/alkaline batteries (EMD electrolytic grade preferred).
Other Mn oxides — MnO, Mn2O3, Mn3O4 used in ferrites and as colourants.
Synthetic Fe2O3 / Fe3O4 / FeO — red ferric, black ferrosoferric, jeweller's rouge.
FeO(OH) / Fe(OH)3 — goethite/limonite; arsenic sorbent in drinking-water treatment.
Earth colours — natural ochres, siennas, umbers containing >=70% combined Fe expressed as Fe2O3 (Note 3 to Ch.28).
CoO / Co3O4 — cobalt-blue pigment (CoO-Al2O3 spinel); ceramic glaze colour.
Co(OH)2 / Co(OH)3 — pink precursor for LCO/NCA cathode materials.
Commercial Co oxide — non-stoichiometric mixed oxide for paints/ceramics.
TiO2 — world's most important white pigment (rutile or anatase polymorph). Produced via sulphate or chloride process.
Other Ti oxides — Ti2O3, Ti3O5 (Magneli phases), TiO sub-oxides.
Litharge — red tetragonal alpha-PbO; major lead-acid battery feedstock.
Massicot — yellow orthorhombic beta-PbO; high-T polymorph.
Pb3O4 (minium / red lead) and PbO2; red lead is anticorrosive primer pigment.
N2H4 anhydrous — monopropellant for satellite thrusters; also a polymerisation inhibitor.
N2H4.H2O — safer to handle than anhydrous; primary commercial form.
N2H6SO4 — stable crystalline salt of hydrazine.
(NH3OH)2SO4 — key intermediate for caprolactam (Nylon-6 monomer).
Other inorganic hydrazine/hydroxylamine salts.
Li2O / LiOH — key precursor for LiFePO4 and NMC cathodes; CO2-absorbent in submarines.
V2O5 flakes — catalyst in Contact-process (SO2 -> SO3) and vanadium redox-flow batteries.
Other V oxides — VO2, V2O3, V3O8, V(OH)x.
NiO / Ni(OH)2 — green/grey solids; Ni(OH)2 is positive-electrode active material in alkaline rechargeable cells.
CuO (black) / Cu2O (red) / Cu(OH)2 (blue) — varied colours; cuprous oxide is antifouling pigment.
GeO2 — high-refractive-index dopant in optical-fibre cores; PET catalyst (preferred over Sb in Asia).
ZrO2 — yttria-stabilised zirconia is the ionic conductor in solid-oxide fuel cells.
MoO3 — white/pale-yellow solid; precursor to molybdate catalysts (ammoxidation, HDS).
H2MoO4 / H2MoO4.H2O — yellow crystals; used in Sonogel chemistry and trace Mo analysis.
Other Mo oxides (MoO2, mixed-valence) and Mo(OH)x.
Sb2O3 — flame-retardant synergist with brominated organics; dominant PET polymerisation catalyst.
SnO2 (cassiterite chemical form) — base material for ITO transparent conductors.
CdO — brown to red-brown; toxic; declining use due to RoHS restrictions.
Ca(OH)2 — slaked lime, distinct from quicklime (CaO) in Ch.25. Saturated solution is limewater.
NH4OH — name for aqueous NH3 in non-IUPAC convention; Indian tariff retains historical name.
Other hydrazines/hydroxylamines and inorganic bases/peroxides not specified above.
AlF3 — bath additive in Hall-Heroult smelting to lower melting point of cryolite.
MgF2 — UV-transparent anti-reflection optical coating; lens material.
Other metal fluorides — NaF, KF, CaF2 (synthetic), LiF, etc.
Na3AlF6 — molten cryolite is the bath in Hall-Heroult Al smelting. Natural cryolite was historically Ch.25 mineral; synthetic = Ch.28.
Complex fluorosalts (fluoroborates, fluorosilicates, fluorotitanates, fluorozirconates).
NH4Cl — electrolyte in Leclanche cells; soldering flux; food-grade ammonium chloride 'salmiak'.
CaCl2 — highly hygroscopic; freezing-point depressant.
MgCl2 — bittern by-product; electrolyte feedstock for Mg-metal production (IG Farben process).
AlCl3 — strong Lewis acid; standard Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation catalyst.
NiCl2 — yellow anhydrous, green hexahydrate; nickel-plating salt.
Hg2Cl2 — historical use as laxative; saturated calomel electrode (SCE) is electrochemistry reference.
SrCl2 — gives crimson flame; active in Sensodyne toothpaste.
CuCl — white solid; Cu(I) salt; catalyst for Sandmeyer aryl-diazonium replacements.
Other metal chlorides (FeCl2/FeCl3, CoCl2, ZnCl2, SnCl2/SnCl4, TiCl4, BaCl2, etc.).
Cu2Cl(OH)3 — green basic copper chloride; major bordeaux-mixture alternative fungicide.
Other Cu oxychloride/chloride-hydroxide compositions.
Other oxychlorides/chloride-hydroxides (BiOCl, SbOCl, ZnOCl, etc.).
NaBr — high-density clear brine for completion fluids; AgBr precursor in photographic emulsions.
KBr — transparent in mid-IR; KBr pellets are classic FTIR sample preparation.
MgBr2 — Lewis acid in synthesis; mild sedative.
Other bromides and bromide oxides (CaBr2, ZnBr2, BaBr2, LiBr).
KI — thyroid blocker in nuclear emergencies; common iodised-salt additive.
NaI — single-crystal NaI(Tl) is the canonical gamma-ray scintillator.
Other iodides and iodide oxides (AgI, CuI, CaI2, ZnI2, PbI2).
Commercial calcium hypochlorite — solid-form chlorine source for pool/water treatment.
Other calcium hypochlorite — purer than commercial bleaching powder.
NaOCl bleaching paste/powder — solid form (rare; most NaOCl trades as solution).
NaOCl solution — household bleach ~5%, industrial ~12-15%; solid form unstable.
KOCl — chlorine-free-from-Na-residue bleach; preferred for some textile applications.
NaClO2 — chlorite (Cl in +III state); precursor for in-situ ClO2 generation.
Al(ClO2)3 — uncommon; sometimes used in textile bleaching baths.
NaOBr — Br analogue of hypochlorite; used in Hofmann rearrangement.
Bleaching paste/powder of other-metal hypochlorites (Mg(OCl)2 etc.).
Other hypohalites/chlorites not separately named.
NaClO3 — produced by brine electrolysis; primary feedstock for ClO2 in ECF pulp bleaching.
Ba(ClO3)2 — gives bright green flame in pyrotechnics.
KClO3 — match-head oxidiser; classical school-lab O2 source (with MnO2 catalyst).
Mg(ClO3)2 — defoliant for cotton harvest.
Other chlorates (NH4ClO3, Ca(ClO3)2, etc.).
NH4ClO4 / KClO4 — solid-rocket booster oxidiser (e.g., Space Shuttle SRBs).
KIO3 / NaIO4 — KIO3 is the modern iodisation agent in table salt; periodate cleaves diols (Malaprade).
Na2S — yellow flakes; key dehairing agent in leather tanning; releases H2S on acidification.
Other metal sulphides — K2S, BaS, CaS, ZnS, CdS (yellow pigment), MoS2 (lubricant).
Na2Sn (n=2-5) and CaSx — precursors to Thiokol polysulphide sealants used in insulating-glass units.
Na2S2O4 — white powder; dominant vat-dye reducer; also food-grade SO2 source (E150d).
Rongalite (HOCH2SO2Na.2H2O) — formaldehyde adduct of sulphoxylate; powerful but mild reducer.
Other dithionite salts — K2S2O4, Zn(S2O4)2.
Other sulphoxylate salts; non-formaldehyde adducts.
NaHSO3 — preservative E222; oxygen scavenger in boilers.
Tariff line uses commercial synonym 'hydrosulphite' for sodium dithionite in HSO3- subheading; legacy nomenclature.
Na2SO3 — neutral sulphite (vs acid sulphite NaHSO3); standard photographic fixer additive.
K2S2O5 — winemaker's standard SO2 source ('Campden tablets').
MgSO3 — pulping reagent in Magnefite process.
Other sulphites — CaSO3, (NH4)2SO3, ZnSO3.
Na2S2O3.5H2O — classic photographic 'hypo' fixer; iodometric titrant.
MgS2O3 — laxative and antibacterial; less common than Na analogue.
Other thiosulphates — (NH4)2S2O3, CaS2O3.
Na2SO4 — 'salt cake' anhydrous or 'Glauber's salt' decahydrate; major commodity.
NaHSO4 / 'sodium bisulphate' — by-product of HCl manufacture; solid acidic alternative to H2SO4.
Na2S2O7 — formed by heating NaHSO4; mineral-fusion flux in analytical chemistry.
Other sodium sulphate forms not separately specified.
MgSO4 — Epsom salt as heptahydrate; pharmaceutical Mg source.
Al2(SO4)3 iron-free — high purity for paper sizing where Fe would discolour.
Standard alum / aluminium sulphate (technical grade, with Fe).
NiSO4 — emerald-green hexahydrate; Watts bath base for Ni electroplating.
CuSO4.5H2O — characteristic blue colour; Bordeaux mixture (with lime).
BaSO4 — synthetic 'blanc fixe' (precipitated); insoluble enough for oral X-ray contrast.
FeSO4.7H2O — green vitriol / copperas; iron-deficiency tablets and Cr(VI) reducer in cement.
Quinidine sulphate — Indian tariff classifies this alkaloid sulphate salt under Ch.28 (vs Ch.29). Tariff-line decision retained.
MnSO4.H2O — pale-pink; precursor for NMC cathode and Mn micronutrient fertiliser.
SrSO4 — celestine chemical form; precursor for SrCO3 (CRT-glass days) and pyrotechnics.
Other sulphates (Co/Zn/Cd/Ag/Hg/Be) not separately specified.
NH4Al(SO4)2.12H2O — double salt; used in pickling-pickle and as baking acid.
NH4Fe(SO4)2.12H2O — Mohr's salt analogue with Fe(III); titration indicator (Volhard method).
KAl(SO4)2.12H2O — classic alum 'phitkari' in India; ancient leather mordant.
Other alums — chrome alum KCr(SO4)2.12H2O, sodium alum NaAl(SO4)2.
(NH4)2S2O8 / Na2S2O8 / K2S2O8 — radical-initiating peroxydisulphate.
NaNO2 — E250 cured-meat preservative; primary diazotising salt.
Other nitrites — KNO2, AgNO2, Ca(NO2)2.
KNO3 — saltpetre; 75% of gunpowder; dual N-K fertiliser; molten salt heat-transfer.
Sr(NO3)2 — gives crimson colour in road flares and fireworks.
Mg(NO3)2.6H2O — drying agent for HNO3 concentration (azeotrope breaking).
Ba(NO3)2 — gives bright green flame; military tracers.
Other nitrates — Bi(NO3)3, Cu(NO3)2, Fe(NO3)3, etc. NB: NH4NO3 + NaNO3 + KNO3 are excluded by Note 2(b) and classified Ch.31 (fertilisers).
Ca(H2PO2)2 — P(I) salt; historically tonic ingredient.
Mg(H2PO2)2 — magnesium phosphinate, used in flame-retardant nylon compounds.
Other hypophosphites/phosphites — NaH2PO2 (Ni-EP), Al phosphite.
NaH2PO4 (MSP) / Na2HPO4 (DSP) — phosphate buffer pair widely used in pharma/food.
KH2PO4 / K2HPO4 / K3PO4 — water-soluble PK fertiliser and buffer salts.
CaHPO4 / CaHPO4.2H2O — DCP; major feed-grade phosphate (brushite mineral form).
Ca(H2PO4)2 — MCP; fast-acting leavening acid in baking powder.
Ca3(PO4)2 — TCP; E341(iii) food additive and bone-substitute precursor.
Other calcium phosphates not separately specified — hydroxyapatite (synthetic).
Mg(H2PO4)2 — soluble Mg-P fertiliser source.
MgHPO4 — dibasic Mg phosphate; mild antacid.
Mg3(PO4)2 — neutral tribasic salt.
(NaPO3)6 — Graham's salt; cyclic metaphosphate; calcium-sequestering water softener.
Other orthophosphates (Zn3(PO4)2, FePO4, AlPO4, ammonium phosphate non-fert).
Na5P3O10 — STPP; dominant detergent builder historically; phased out in EU/US due to eutrophication.
Other polyphosphates — tetrasodium pyrophosphate (TSPP), potassium tripolyphosphate.
Na2CO3 dense — granular, free-flowing, used in glass batch.
Na2CO3 light — lower bulk density; preferred in detergents/dyes.
Other Na2CO3 forms — monohydrate (thermonatrite), decahydrate (washing soda).
NaHCO3 — Solvay-process intermediate; ubiquitous baking soda.
K2CO3 — 'pearl ash' historically from wood lye; soft-glass component; drying agent for amines.
CaCO3 — synthetic/precipitated (PCC) or ground (GCC); world's most-used mineral filler. Note: natural limestone in Ch.25.
BaCO3 — toxic if soluble; sulphate scavenger in clay bricks.
Li2CO3 — globally critical mineral; precursor for cathode-grade Li compounds.
SrCO3 — major use historically in CRT glass to block X-rays; now ferrite magnets.
Sodium percarbonate (2Na2CO3.3H2O2) — Oxiclean active; release H2O2 in water.
MgCO3 — gymnast/climber chalk; mild laxative.
Al(HCO3)3 — unstable in pure form; usually basic aluminium carbonate gel.
Other carbonates — basic carbonates of Zn/Cu/Ni; ammonium carbonate/bicarbonate.
NaCN — extremely toxic; primary gold-mining leachant via Au + 2CN- + 1/4O2 + 1/2H2O -> Au(CN)2- + OH-.
KCN — alternative to NaCN; preferred for gold/silver plating baths.
Mixed K-Na cyanide salt; used in case-hardening of steel.
Other cyanides and cyanide oxides — Ca(CN)2, Zn(CN)2, AgCN, AuCN.
NH4SCN — Fe(III) gives blood-red Fe(SCN)3 colorimetric test.
K3[Fe(CN)6] — bright red crystals; Hill-Lambert blueprint chemistry; mild oxidiser despite cyanide ligands.
K4[Fe(CN)6].3H2O — yellow prussiate of potash; food-grade anti-caking agent in iodised salt.
Na4[Fe(CN)6] — yellow prussiate of soda; ferrocyanide ion non-toxic despite name.
Na2[Fe(CN)5(NO)].2H2O — releases NO in vivo; emergency BP control. Sulphide detection reagent (purple).
Other complex cyanides — Ag/Au/Cu cyanide complexes used in plating.
Na2SiO3 — heavy-duty alkaline cleaner; cement-set retarder.
Other Na silicates of varying SiO2:Na2O ratios; commonly viscous aqueous solutions.
Mg2Si3O8.xH2O — slow-acting non-systemic antacid (Gaviscon component).
Other silicates — K-silicate, lithium silicate, lead silicate.
Na2B4O7 — anhydrous borax; high-purity glass and ceramic flux.
Na2B4O7.10H2O / .5H2O — common laundry borax in hydrated form.
Mg borates — used in fibreglass and as smoke-suppressant flame retardant.
Other borates — Zn, K, Cu, Ca borates; mostly flame-retardants.
NaBO3.H2O / .4H2O — sodium perborate; in-situ H2O2 release during washing; phased down in Europe due to boron concerns.
Na2Cr2O7 — orange Cr(VI) salt; restricted under REACH Authorisation List.
Na2CrO4 — yellow Cr(VI) salt; dichromate is its acid form.
Other Cr(VI) salts — K2CrO4/K2Cr2O7, (NH4)2Cr2O7, lead/zinc chromates (pigments).
KMnO4 — dark purple crystals; iron removal in drinking water; classic Baeyer test oxidant.
Other Mn oxyanion salts — NaMnO4 (more soluble than KMnO4), K2MnO4 (green Mn(VI)).
Al2(MoO4)3 — uncommon; specialty catalyst applications.
Na2MoO4 — non-chromate corrosion inhibitor in closed-loop systems.
Other molybdates — (NH4)6Mo7O24 (ammonium heptamolybdate / 'paramolybdate'), Ca/Pb/Zn molybdates.
Na2WO4 — water-soluble W source; key APT (ammonium paratungstate) intermediate.
MgWO4 — bluish-white phosphor; X-ray intensifying screen luminophore.
Other tungstates — APT (NH4)10(W12O41).5H2O, CaWO4 (scheelite chemical form), PbWO4 (scintillator).
Other salts of metal oxoacids — aluminates, antimonates, vanadates, titanates, zirconates, plumbates, ferrites.
Synthetic zeolites — Zeolite A, Y, ZSM-5; framework alumino-silicates used in FCC and detergents (replacing STPP).
AsO3(3-) / AsO4(3-) salts — historically used as 'Paris Green' Cu(II) acetoarsenite insecticide; now restricted.
Bichromates/dichromates of inorganic acids per heading 2842 (not the 2841 line) — e.g., Pb chromate-dichromate basic salts.
Other salts/peroxysalts of inorganic acids/peroxoacids not elsewhere classified — fulminates, cyanates, selenites, tellurites.
Colloidal Au — red-burgundy nanoparticle suspension; lateral-flow assay labels; Haruta catalyst.
Colloidal Ag — yellow-brown nanoparticle suspension; antimicrobial properties.
Other colloidal PGMs — colloidal Pt, Pd, Rh, Ir, Ru, Os.
AgNO3 — primary Ag source; halide-precipitation Mohr titration.
Other Ag compounds — AgCl/AgBr/AgI (light-sensitive emulsions), Ag2O, Ag2CO3, silver oxide batteries.
HAuCl4 (chloroauric acid), AuCl3, Na3Au(S2O3)2 — water-gilding and chrysotherapy Au(I) drugs.
Na3[Au(S2O3)2].2H2O — 'Sanocrysin'; cyanide-free Au plating bath for jewellery.
Other PGM compounds — chloroplatinic acid H2PtCl6, PdCl2, RhCl3, IrCl3 — catalyst feedstocks.
Amalgams of precious metals (Au/Ag amalgam) — dental amalgam Hg-Ag-Sn-Cu alloy.
Natural U (0.72% U-235); compounds UO2, U3O8 (yellowcake), UF4, UF6, alloys, cermets, ceramic fuel pellets.
LEU/HEU and Pu — controlled under NSG/IAEA safeguards; reactor and weapons material.
DU — by-product of U-235 enrichment; very dense (19.1 g/cm3); used in KE penetrator rounds. Th metal for incandescent gas mantles historically.
ThO2 — highest melting point of any oxide (3390 deg C); Welsbach mantle historical use.
Th(OH)4 — intermediate in monazite processing.
Th(NO3)4 — water-soluble; impregnated cotton mantles ignited then dipped to give incandescent Welsbach mantle.
Other Th compounds — ThF4, ThCl4, ThO(NO3)2.
DU / Th waste and scrap — recovered for reuse.
Other DU/Th forms — alloys, dispersions, cermets, ceramic products and mixtures.
T (H-3) — 12.3 yr half-life beta emitter; self-illuminating gun sights; biological tracer.
Specifically listed alpha-emitting/short-half-life radioisotopes (Ac-225 etc.) — targeted alpha therapy and neutron sources (Cf-252).
Other radioisotopes/compounds — Mo-99/Tc-99m, I-131, Co-60, Cs-137, Ir-192.
Radioactive residues — HLW vitrification feed, contaminated process residues.
SNF — spent fuel assemblies; PUREX reprocessing feedstock or once-through disposal.
D2O — India is leading producer for PHWR fleet; CIRUS/Dhruva moderator.
B-10 enriched — very high neutron-capture cross-section; reactor control rods.
Li-6 enriched — breeds T from neutron capture (Li-6 + n -> T + alpha) in fusion blankets.
He-3 — extremely rare; from tritium decay; supply crisis ~2010 due to security applications.
Catch-all for nuclear fuels not elsewhere included/specified.
Other stable/enriched isotopes — C-13, N-15, O-18, Mo-100, Xe-129; non-radioactive enriched.
CeO2 — Ce(IV)/Ce(III) redox couple stores O2 in TWC catalysts; precision glass-polishing powder.
Other Ce compounds — CeF3, CeCl3, Ce2(CO3)3, Ce(NO3)3 — precursors.
Other rare-earth oxides not specified — Nd2O3, Pr6O11, Sm2O3, Eu2O3 (red phosphor), Y2O3, Tb4O7, Dy2O3.
REF3 (e.g., NdF3, DyF3) — calciothermic reduction feed for rare-earth metals.
RECl3.xH2O (Nd, La, Y, Ce chlorides) — typical solvent-extraction feed in RE separation.
Other RE compounds — nitrates, carbonates, oxalates, acetates of Sc/Y/lanthanides.
H2O2 — typically 30-50% aqueous (commercial); urea adduct CH4N2O.H2O2 ('carbamide peroxide') for dental/topical use.
CaC2 — reacts with water to release C2H2; mining-lamp fuel historically; cyanamide precursor.
SiC carborundum — Mohs 9.5 abrasive; Acheson-process synthesis; emerging power-electronics wide-bandgap semiconductor (typo in tariff: 'Carborandum').
Other SiC forms — green/black grades by purity.
B4C — 3rd-hardest material (Mohs 9.5+); body-armour plates and reactor shut-down rods.
WC — second-hardest metal compound after diamond; bonded with Co into 'cemented carbide' cutters.
Other carbides — TiC, TaC, NbC, ZrC, Cr3C2, VC, Mo2C — cermet and cutting-tool components.
LiH/NaH/CaH2/LiAlH4/NaBH4 — workhorse reductants in organic chemistry.
Si3N4 / AlN / BN / GaN / TiN — high-T ceramics; cBN (cubic BN) is second-hardest material.
NaN3 — airbag inflator; Pb(N3)2 — primary explosive in detonators.
CaSi2 — steel deoxidiser delivering both Ca and Si simultaneously.
Other silicides — MoSi2 (heating elements), FeSi, TiSi2, WSi2 (semiconductor interconnects).
TiB2 / ZrB2 / HfB2 / LaB6 — ultra-high-T ceramics; LaB6 is thermionic emitter.
Chemically defined Hg compounds — HgCl2 (corrosive sublimate), HgO, HgS (cinnabar synthetic), Hg(NO3)2; Minamata Convention restricted.
Non-chemically-defined Hg compounds — mixtures, dispersions, mercurochrome-type.
ClCN — CWA Schedule 3; pseudohalogen pungent and toxic; cyanuric chloride precursor.
H2O distilled/conductivity grade — Ch.28 covers purified water; natural waters are Ch.22.
Liquid air — feed for cryogenic air-separation units (ASU).
Compressed air — pneumatic working fluid.
Amalgams of base metals — Na/K amalgams (chlor-alkali Castner cell), Zn amalgam (Clemmensen).
Mg3P2 / Zn3P2 — release lethal PH3 on contact with moisture; grain-store fumigant ('Celphos').
Other inorganic compounds of Ch.28 residual basket; includes cyanates, fulminates, halogen oxides, etc.
